_what_this_is: Indian income tax, as data rather than as numbers typed into a calculation. Every figure compare_tax_regimes.py uses comes from this file, so C4 is satisfied structurally: the number traces to a source file, and the source file says where it came from.
_the_rule_that_matters: These are the rates for the financial year named in `financial_year` below. Slabs change with every Union Budget, usually in February. If `financial_year` is not the year you are filing for, every figure computed from this file is out of date and INKY says so on the report rather than quietly using stale rates.
source: Finance Act 2025, as passed. New-regime slabs and the raised 87A rebate were announced in the Union Budget presented 2025-02-01.
_verified_note: Owner-confirmed 2026-09-06: FY2025-26, new regime, and the zero-tax outcome for ~10L salary income (full 87A rebate up to 12L total income). Slabs and the raised rebate match the Finance Act 2025 as passed. Re-open and re-check against incometax.gov.in when financial_year rolls to 2026-27 (Union Budget ~Feb 2026).

new.label: New regime (Section 115BAC) - the default since FY 2023-24

rebate_87a._note: Income up to 12,00,000 after the standard deduction pays no tax at all. For a salaried person that is 12,75,000 of salary. Just above the line, marginal relief caps the tax at the amount by which income exceeds 12,00,000.

new._deductions_note: This is the half people get wrong. Under the new regime 80C, 80D, 80E, 80TTA and the self-occupied 24(b) interest are ALL unavailable. Only the employer's NPS contribution under 80CCD(2) and the standard deduction survive. A person carrying a big education loan or a big 80C basket has a genuine decision to make; a person with neither does not.

old.label: Old regime - must be opted into

cess.name: Health and Education Cess
cess._note: Charged on tax AFTER rebate, in both regimes.

surcharge._note: The new regime caps surcharge at 25%. The old regime goes to 37% above 5 crore.

what_counts: Tuition fees for up to two children
80C._note: One shared 1,50,000 ceiling across all of the above, not one each. Most salaried people fill a large part of it with EPF before choosing anything.

80CCD(1B)._note: Sits on top of 80C, so the combined ceiling is 2,00,000.

80CCD(2)._note: The only meaningful deduction that survives into the new regime. It costs the employee nothing directly - it is the employer routing part of CTC into NPS.

what_counts: Interest on an education loan - interest only, never principal
80E._note: No monetary ceiling at all: the whole interest is deductible. Available for 8 assessment years starting from the year repayment begins, or until the interest is fully paid, whichever is earlier. Only for a loan from a bank or an approved financial institution - a loan from a relative does not qualify, which matters when somebody is carrying both.

24(b)._note: A let-out property has no ceiling on the interest itself, but the loss that can be set off against other heads is capped at 2,00,000 a year.

listed_equity_and_equity_mutual_funds._note: The 1,25,000 exemption is per financial year and per person, and it does not carry forward. Gains not booked before 31 March are gains whose exemption was thrown away.

debt_mutual_funds_bought_on_or_after_202._note: Section 50AA. There is no long-term rate for these at all - every gain is added to income and taxed at the person's own slab, however long it was held.

immovable_property._note: For property acquired before 23 July 2024, a resident individual may instead choose 20% with indexation, whichever is lower.

_what_this_file_does_not_cover: Surcharge marginal relief arithmetic above 50 lakh
HUF, firm and company rates - this is an individual's file
Presumptive taxation under 44AD / 44ADA for freelance and professional income
Advance tax instalment dates and interest under 234B / 234C
